reviews.reason: changes: section 16 gains the owner rule of 2026-11-13, "always attempt native component from fluentui components before attempting a rewrite": a new bullet after the raw-element bullet requires starting from the Fluent v9 component and shaping it through its props, slots, variants and makeStyles, makes a bespoke re-implementation of a control Fluent already provides a defect in the same way a raw element is, requires the round doc to name the Fluent component tried and why it was rejected, disqualifies "it did not look right" by name, and carves out a hand-drawn mock while refusing the same in production code. why: the owner asked for the rule after the page-actions surface raised the question of whether to compose Fluent Menu primitives or hand-build a menu, and section 16 covered only raw elements, not rewrites, so a bespoke control could pass review while forking focus, keyboard and ARIA behaviour the library already gets right. rejected: leaving it to section 15 alone (which governs extraction and wrapping, not re-implementation); recording the rule only in the round doc (an ephemeral artifact); the first wording, which said "native component" and "Start from the Fluent v9 component" unconditionally - the review found that this repo already means raw HTML by "native" (imports-ui-shell.md) and that the imperative bound composites with no Fluent counterpart, so the text now reads "the Fluent component" and "When Fluent provides the control, start from it and shape it". The two owner-gated strengthenings were answered "all as recommended" and are in this text rather than left open: a rejected rewrite must cite a documented gap with its link or a reproducible blocker (awkwardness is not a limitation, and appearance belongs in props, slots and tokens), and a hand-built control where Fluent provides one is a blocking (P1) review finding, not a taste note. A third review round accepted both: P1 is already this repository's word for a blocking finding (the reviewer contract's "P1 (must fix)", and the merge policy's "resolves every P1 before the PR"), so the rule borrows the established severity rather than minting one.
